children: Decade-high almond prices have put nut farmer Select Harvests in a good spot, according to its bull at Bell Potter. With an unchanged buy rating on the stock, analyst Jonathan Snape tells clients in a note that ASX-listed Select Harvests has begun its 2027 fiscal year with a mature orchard base and a low level of debt, while key input cost inflation appears to be easing. He adds that the company's debt is more than covered by carry-out crop volumes. Snape sees the 20% valuation discount to net asset value as excessive, and its 10.8x earnings multiple as undemanding. Bell Potter raises its target price by 5.0% to 6.35 Australian dollars. Shares are up 3.75% at A$4.98. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
